items.headline: [Helsinki Analytic Theology Workshop 2027 — Religious Experience CFP, deadline 14 September 2026](https://blogs.helsinki.fi/analytictheology/)
items.summary: The University of Helsinki Faculty of Theology is accepting abstracts for HEAT2027 on Religious Experience. The workshop will take place in Helsinki on 24–26 February 2027. The call welcomes graduate students and researchers from theology, philosophy and related fields; abstracts are due 14 September 2026.
items.why_it_matters: A current Helsinki-based doctoral development opportunity that could be relevant if Rukhsar frames work around religious experience, scripture, interpretation, reception or contextual theology. The official page gives the submission instructions and contact details.
items.source: University of Helsinki — Helsinki Analytic Theology Workshop

items.headline: [Women in Eastern Orthodoxy — pastoral and liturgical participation, Helsinki 2–3 November 2026](https://www.uef.fi/fi/tapahtuma/women-in-eastern-orthodoxy-questions-of-pastoral-and-liturgical-participation)
items.summary: The University of Eastern Finland School of Theology, Helsinki Collegium for Advanced Studies and the Orthodox Church of Finland are organising an international academic conference in Helsinki on 2–3 November 2026 about women in Eastern Orthodoxy, focusing on pastoral and liturgical participation. Audience registration is available through the official event page.
items.why_it_matters: Strongly aligned with Rukhsar's interests in gender, theology, church contexts and the interpretation of women's roles in religious traditions, while also offering a Finland-based networking opportunity.

items.headline: [The Oxford Handbook of King David — new Hebrew Bible volume with gender, violence and reception-history chapters](https://academic.oup.com/edited-volume/63159)
items.summary: Oxford University Press published The Oxford Handbook of King David online on 24 July 2026, with the print edition due 16 September 2026. The volume includes chapters on David's masculinity in the Hebrew Bible, sexual violence in the David story, women such as Abigail and Michal, and reception of David across Judaism, Christianity, Islam and the arts.
items.why_it_matters: This is a highly relevant recent scholarly resource for Rukhsar's methodological interests in gendered interpretation, suffering/violence, Hebrew Bible studies and reception history, even though its primary biblical focus is David rather than Hosea.

items.headline: [New discussion of Hosea 6:7 and the meaning of the covenant reference](https://heidelblog.net/2026/09/on-hosea-67-and-the-covenant-of-works/)
items.summary: A new article published today revisits Hosea 6:7 and the interpretive question whether the text means 'like Adam', 'like men', or refers to a place called Adam. It is useful as a current example of how translation, covenant language and textual interpretation continue to shape Hosea scholarship.
items.why_it_matters: Directly relevant to Rukhsar's Hosea research because it shows a live interpretive debate around wording, metaphor and theological reception in Hosea. 🔗 Click the title above to open the source.

items.headline: [Upcoming Helsinki lecture: The Suppressed Mother — Sarah and Khadijah in Muslim and Jewish traditions](https://blogs.helsinki.fi/islamic-studies-and-theology/news-activities/middle-east-and-islamic-studies-lecture-series/public-lecture-series-program-2026-27/)
items.summary: The University of Helsinki's 2026/27 public lecture series lists a Zoom lecture for 17 September 2026 at 16:00–18:00. The official page contains the Zoom registration information.
items.why_it_matters: Highly relevant to Rukhsar's interest in gendered interpretation, reception history and the treatment of female figures across religious traditions. 🔗 Click the title above for the official University of Helsinki page and registration information.

items.headline: [New Approaches to Biblical Literary Studies — open call, deadline 30 September 2026](https://www.mdpi.com/journal/humanities/special_issue_flyer_pdf_v2/B3Q652GS13)
items.summary: The Humanities special issue New Approaches to Biblical Literary Studies is currently open for manuscript submissions, with a deadline of 30 September 2026. Its scope includes Bible and literature, scripture, hermeneutics, Jewish–Christian relations, biblical allusion, Tanak, and Old and New Testaments.
items.why_it_matters: Potentially useful for Rukhsar's work on Hosea, metaphor, gender, reception and literary interpretation. 🔗 Click the title above to see the call and submission scope.
items.source: Humanities / MDPI; also listed by Society of Biblical Literature

items.headline: [UEF OCREA conference — minorities, women and identity in religious education](https://sites.uef.fi/ocrea20/conference-programme/)
items.summary: The University of Eastern Finland's OCREA 20th-anniversary conference runs 2–4 September 2026 in Joensuu. The programme includes papers on Roma women in religious education, minority teachers, identity markers and religious educational spaces.
items.why_it_matters: Relevant to Rukhsar's wider profile in theology, education, gender, minority Christianity and contextual/reception-oriented work. 🔗 Click the title above for the UEF conference programme.
